To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resting site selection by mosquito pupae is influenced by behavioral mechanisms.

pupae of Aedes and Culex species rest in concave water menisci associated with vertical surfaces, and that they dive less frequently and terminate diving more quickly in these resting sites, compared to open water.

pupae of Ae. aegyptii, Ae. trisieritus and Cx. restuans rest in concave water menisci associated with submerged vertical surfaces, and that this resting site selection behavior is mediated by a behavioral mechanism that minimizes the amount of energy expended in the diving behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavior of aquatic organisms and their interactions with their environment.
the behavioral ecology of mosquito pupae.
the behavioral mechanisms that influence the resting-site selection of aquatic insect larvae and pupae.

pupal resting site selection is a behavioral mechanism by which pupae of three mosquito species avoid diving and increase their chances of surfac- ing in a meniscus.
